corpusSummary: Across 2026 records, the corpus chronicles how LLMs and AI tools are studied in real use, governance, and social contexts. It documents evaluation frameworks for deployment, equity-focused governance in health, education and policy, LLMs as research instruments with validation challenges, and nuanced human–AI interactions spanning trust, embodiment, and social influence, alongside concerns about bias, safety, and misinformation.

themes.name: Real-world AI deployment, evaluation, and governance
themes.description: Empirical and framework-based studies examine deployment decisions, contextual consequences, governance, and equity implications across organizational, health, and policy domains.

themes.name: LLMs as social science research tools and methodological challenges
themes.description: A spectrum of works explores using LLMs and multi-agent LLM systems for data extraction, analysis, simulation, and theory-building, while highlighting validation, bias, and ethical constraints.

themes.name: Human–AI interaction, trust, embodiment, and social influence
themes.description: Research investigates how users perceive AI advice, trust AI, experience embodiment, and respond to social cues in education, health, and everyday decision-making.

themes.name: AI in health, education, and wellbeing: safety, literacy, and equity
themes.description: A cluster of studies focuses on AI-enabled health information, patient education, mental health, literacy, and governance aimed at fairness, accessibility, and readability.

emergingKeywords: multi-agent LLM systems in social science
